lines: Five lanes. Five today. That is the rule.
Everything that owns a piece of your day, in one place.
What is on the bench, and only that.
bodies: Five lanes from idea to done, with a hard cap of five items on Today so the day stays a day.
Planner tasks and tool items land here as cards, and Today never holds more than five of them.
One board, fed by Planner and the four TomFit tools, so nothing lives only in someone else's inbox.
Five lanes, one cap: Today takes five, and the rest waits its turn until there is room.

lines: Order it before it is late.
What you are waiting on, and who is holding it.
Parts arrive on their schedule, not yours.
bodies: Every item gets an order-by date worked back from its lead time, so the deadline you see is the one that matters.
A list of parts and requests, each with the day you must order it and the person it is currently waiting on.
Lead time in, order-by date out, with a separate view of everything sitting with a supplier or a colleague.
Procurement tracks what needs ordering, when it becomes too late, and which items are blocked on other people.

lines: The tools you already use, without the tabs.
bodies: Issue tickets, the QMS, the structured BOM and Phase Gate are read directly from the TomFit tools, no export step.
Sign in once per tool and Bench. pulls your open items from Issue tickets, QMS, structured BOM and Phase Gate.
The four TomFit tools stay the system of record; Bench. only reads what is assigned to you and shows it on the board.
Each tool keeps its own login, you sign in once, and from then on your items appear here without copying.

lines: The company view, one window over.
Zoom out when you need to.
bodies: The TomFit Cockpit is the company overview dashboard, opened in its own window so it does not crowd the bench.
Cockpit shows the wider TomFit picture and keeps your sign-in, so it is one click away rather than one login away.
A separate window for the company dashboard, with your session kept so you can glance at it and come back.
Cockpit is the TomFit overview; Bench. opens it beside the board and remembers you are signed in.

lines: Who said what, and what follows.
bodies: One entry per meeting: who was there, what was decided, what someone has to do next. Actions go to the board with a click and keep a line back here.
Notes from the room, in the order they happened. Decisions on one side, actions on the other, and a search that finds the sentence you half remember.
A place for meeting notes that does not become a second task list: the actions leave for the board, the context stays.
Dated entries, attendees, decisions, actions. Nothing more, and it is enough.

lines: The back of the napkin, kept.
bodies: Mind maps that lay themselves out. One idea in the middle, branches on both sides, Tab for a child, Enter for the next thought.
For the part of the work that is not a list yet. Draw the shape of a problem, fold what is settled, come back when it is time to decide.
A quick canvas for thinking out loud. Every branch is editable in place and the map keeps itself tidy.
Where a wiring concept, a supplier question or a test plan starts, before any of it is a task.

about.short: The day was spread across five tools. This is the one place it all shows at once.
about.long: Bench. exists because the pieces of the day were spread across five tools, and none of them showed the whole bench at once. It runs locally and keeps everything in a folder you choose. Noël built it at TomFit for his own bench first; if it helps yours too, good.
about.footer: Runs on this machine, nothing in a cloud of its own. The board lives in a folder you choose; your hours, sign-ins and settings stay in your own profile. It talks to Microsoft 365 and the TomFit tools, and to nothing else.

firstRun.title: Before we start.
firstRun.body: Your name, as the tools spell it, for the greeting and to match what Issues, QMS and the BOM assign to you. A work email too, because the tools sometimes list people by address. Nothing is sent anywhere.
firstRun.nameLabel: Name, as the tools spell it
firstRun.connectBody: Bench. reads your Planner tasks and writes your hours into the Zeiterfassung workbook through Microsoft 365. Connect now and it is ready when you open the bench; skip and the button waits in Settings.
